value.body: State health departments recruit ANMs, also called Multi-Purpose Health Workers (Female), for sub-health centres, Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and primary health centres. The work covers antenatal and postnatal care, immunisation, family planning and keeping health records for a village or ward population. Posts are either regular state posts or contractual posts under the National Health Mission (NHM).

items.label: Basic requirement
items.note: Registered with the State Nursing Council; some states also accept GNM

items.label: Who recruits
items.value: State recruitment boards, health departments or NHM district health societies

items.label: Sub-health centres
items.note: ~1.66 lakh rural and ~4,000 urban; the norm is at least one ANM per sub-centre
items.source: MoHFW, Health Dynamics of India (Infrastructure & Human Resources) 2022-23 (as reported)

items.label: Health workers at sub-centres
items.note: Male and female health workers combined; not an ANM-only count
items.source: MoHFW, Health Dynamics of India (Infrastructure & Human Resources) 2022-23 (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Complete the ANM diploma and register with the State Nursing Council. Apply to the state's ANM or MPHW (Female) recruitment, usually a written test and document verification, or to NHM contract notices from the state or district health society. Many states require the local language and give weight to domicile.

value.title: At a glance
items: Contract posts under NHM are more frequent than regular posts; terms differ by state.
Postings are usually rural, with field visits to homes and outreach sessions.
Promotion in some states is to Lady Health Visitor or health supervisor.

value.title: Students enrolled in the ANM course, by year
value.note: A.N.M. (Auxiliary Nurse & Midwife) row of the programme-wise table. This is the qualifying course for these posts, not a count of posts or vacancies. Many ANM schools may not report to AISHE. AISHE counts only institutions that responded to the survey; coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11 programme-wise enrolment (all modes), actual responses (Ministry of Education)
